finding.claim: /preview proxies an arbitrary attacker-supplied URL with no validation and reflects the status code and first 500 characters of the response body to the caller.
finding.source: Query parameter 'url' read at app.py:15 via request.args.get("url", ""); supplied by any remote client.
finding.sink: requests.get(target, timeout=5) at app.py:16; response returned via jsonify at app.py:17.

trace.note: Attacker-controlled 'url' query parameter assigned to target without modification.
Server issues GET to target with requests; no scheme, host, IP-range, or port check; redirects followed by default.
resp.status_code and resp.text[:500] returned to the caller, so responses from internal hosts are readable.

finding.guards_checked: None on the path. No scheme, host, IP-range, port, or redirect restrictions anywhere in app.py. No tests or config present in the repo.

verdict.guard_found: none. The ALLOWED_HOSTS allowlist (app.py:9) and host check (app.py:23-25) apply only to the /partner route. /preview (app.py:13-17) has no validation before requests.get at app.py:16.
verdict.reason: The attacker-controlled 'url' query parameter at app.py:15 flows unchecked into requests.get at app.py:16, and the status code and first 500 characters of the body are returned at app.py:17; the only host allowlist (app.py:24) is on the separate /partner route.

finding.claim: /partner allowlist checks only the initial URL's hostname; requests follows redirects to arbitrary hosts, so an allowlisted host that redirects can reach internal addresses (blind SSRF with status-code oracle).
finding.source: Query parameter 'url' read at app.py:22; supplied by any remote client.
finding.sink: requests.get(target, timeout=5) at app.py:26, with default allow_redirects=True.

trace.note: host = urlparse(target).hostname computed for the check.
host compared against ALLOWED_HOSTS (defined at app.py:9); only the first URL is validated.
requests.get(target) follows any 3xx Location to any host; destination is never re-checked.
Only resp.status_code returned, making the attack blind but still an oracle for internal reachability.

finding.guards_checked: Hostname allowlist at app.py:23-25 (applies to initial URL only). No scheme check, no allow_redirects=False, no per-hop re-validation, no IP-range check. Effectiveness depends on whether an allowlisted partner host has an open redirect, which the repo cannot confirm.

verdict.guard_found: Exact hostname set membership at app.py:23-24 (urlparse(target).hostname checked against ALLOWED_HOSTS, defined at app.py:9). It validates only the initial URL. No allow_redirects=False at app.py:26, no per-hop re-check, and no IP-range check. The guard does not cover redirect hops, so it does not close this redirect-based claim.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: target is taken from the query string at app.py:22, the hostname is checked once at app.py:23-24, and requests.get(target, timeout=5) at app.py:26 follows redirects by default, so any redirect from an allowlisted host to an internal address is fetched and its status code is returned at app.py:27. Exploitation still depends on an allowlisted partner host returning a redirect (open redirect or compromise), which this repo cannot confirm, so the impact is conditional. Separately, /preview at app.py:15-16 has no allowlist at all, which is a stronger finding that the candidate does not mention.

finding.claim: Possible parser differential between urllib.parse.urlparse (used for the allowlist check) and urllib3 (used by requests to send the request) could let a URL pass the check while requests connects to a different host.
finding.source: Query parameter 'url' read at app.py:22; supplied by any remote client.

trace.note: Host extracted with urlparse, e.g. 'https://evil.example\@api.partner.example/' yields hostname 'api.partner.example'.
Check passes because the parsed host is allowlisted.
requests/urllib3 may parse the host as 'evil.example'; unverified, as no code could be executed and behavior varies by version.

finding.guards_checked: Hostname allowlist at app.py:23-25. The check and the request use different parsers, and no normalization or re-parsing is applied before the request.

verdict.guard_found: app.py:23-24: `host = urlparse(target).hostname` followed by `if host not in ALLOWED_HOSTS`, an exact membership check on the parsed hostname against {"api.partner.example", "cdn.partner.example"}, which is one of the closing guards the policy names.
verdict.reason: The source is attacker-controlled (app.py:22), but the exact-hostname set membership check at app.py:23-24 is a closing guard, and the parser-differential claim at app.py:26 is speculation that the code cannot confirm, so the finding does not hold.
